title: Cadence: Leadership Handoff Scratchpad
agenda: Pricing experiment: early signals and decision target (8m)
Dedicated capacity sales motion: blockers and escalations (7m)
content:
Purpose: rapid handoff for tomorrow's exec staff sync — focus on decisions we need to make this cycle and immediate escalations. This is a working scratchpad; bullets are shorthand.

Context/what I want from this meeting:
- Confirm go/no-go on two mitigations for the EU-dedicated region latency spike (auto-fallback + tighter batching window). Need explicit owner for rollout and rollback plan.
- Decide whether to pause the new pricing experiment for small customers until we validate QoS on mixed workloads.
- Surface any sales/legal blockers for Dedicated contracts requiring on-prem KMS — we have 2 deals in flight that need a decision this quarter.

High-level metrics (latest):
- Hosted API 99th latency (p95/p99) last 48h: 180ms / 420ms (EU region spike on 2026-03-06).
- Dedicated pool utilization (prod): 76% overall; EU pool at 92% during peak windows.
- Unit cost impact if we enable tighter batching + fallback: projected +6% latency, -12% cost per token (est).
- Active Dedicated trials: 7 (2 enterprise with KMS asks).

Key talking points / suggested scripts:
- Reliability update: "We observed a short-lived degradation in the EU Dedicated pool tied to a kernel scheduling regression on 03-06. The short-term mitigation is to enable model-variant fallback and reduce batch-window by 15ms. Ops has a rollback ready if the fallback causes quality regressions."
- Pricing experiment: "Initial signals show higher error rate on small mixed workloads — recommending a temporary pause for the cohort while we instrument more granular QoS metrics."
- Sales/legal escalation: "Two enterprise pilots require on-prem KMS; ask: approve scope to provision Private deployment pilot + legal checklist sign-off by 03-17."

Risks & friction (prioritized):
1) EU Dedicated saturation: risk of repeat spike if traffic patterns persist during peak. Mitigation: short-term fallback + medium-term scale-up commit. Owner: Jon.
2) Model-quality regression when fallback to quantized variant: present in 1-in-1000 prompts. Mitigation: limited canary, A/B prompt set evals. Owner: Priya.
3) Pricing confusion with small customers if experiment paused mid-flight. Mitigation: comms template + credits. Owner: Aisha.

Open questions for execs:
- Are we comfortable authorizing a 10% short-term capacity add for EU to cover next 4 weeks? (cost vs SLA tradeoff)
- Can legal sign off on a limited-scope Private pilot with KMS by 03-17? If not, what is the blocker?
- Does GTM want us to pause the pricing experiment across all cohorts or just small customers?

Decisions needed (explicit asks):
- Decision 1: Approve EU emergency capacity + fallback plan (Yes/No). Target decision window: today.
- Decision 2: Pause pricing experiment for small customers until additional QoS gating is implemented (Approve/Pause).
- Decision 3: Authorize Private/KMS pilot scope and expedited legal review.

Draft comms snippets (ops -> eng / cs):
- Ops -> Eng: "We're enabling fallback in EU for 24–72h starting now; monitor model quality metrics and flag any >0.5% regression immediately."
- CS -> Customers: "We are applying a temporary adjustment in the EU region to improve reliability; you may see small changes in latency as we stabilize. Reach out to your CSM for impact review."

Follow-ups (format: Owner — Task — Due):
- Jon Kim — Execute EU fallback + capacity add runbook; confirm rollback steps — 2026-03-11
- Priya Desai — Run A/B eval on quantized variant against our prompt set; report regressions and thresholds — 2026-03-12
- Aisha Patel — Draft pricing experiment pause comms & coordinate with GTM; ensure customer credit ledger updated — 2026-03-12
- Liam O'Connor — Prepare legal checklist for Private/KMS pilot; surface any unacceptable clauses — 2026-03-15
- Ops oncall (TBD) — Post-mortem doc stub and timeline for root-cause — 2026-03-14

Notes to self / meeting tactics:
- Start with the EU incident; keep it tight (8–10m) and avoid deep kernel-level debate in exec forum. Redline asks only.
- Use the pricing experiment signal to push GTM to choose (pause vs continue) — prepare visual of error-rate vs revenue impact.
- If Legal can't meet 03-17, propose a narrow pilot with a technical isolation clause to unblock sales.

Appendix (short):
- Quick links: incident runbook (confluence link above), Dedicated pool dashboard (dashboards/redwood/dedicated-eu), pricing-experiment notebook (github.com/redwood/pricing-experiments/epic-23).
- Last callouts from yesterday: support ticket cluster 4721 shows concentration in three customers; flagged for targeted outreach.

End of scratchpad. Will trim for exec deck and surface 3 clear asks at meeting start.
